newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Rare China deal to emerge.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Rare China deal to emerge.

text.p: Asian debt market was quiet on the last Friday of 1996 amid the year-end vacations.
But syndicate managers in Asia said a string of new issues are expected to come on stream in the near future.
China Construction Holdings's debut three-year US$30 million floating rate note issue is rumoured to emerge next week.
The issue is likely to be priced at par to float at 200 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR), sources said.
They said the price talk for the deal is between 215 to 225 basis points.
BA Asia and KorAm Bank were tipped to have won the mandate. But none of the banks were immediately available for comment.
There is no guarantor for the issue, sources said. Instead, China's Ministry of Construction will offer a letter of undertaking for the deal.
The issuer is an associate company of the ministry.
The high-yield paper is expected to meet with warm reception especially from Korean-based financial insitutions operating on relatively high funding costs.
These institutions are looking to extend their investment portfolio from Thailand and Indonesia, to other high-yield countries like China and the Philippines, a syndicate manager said.
However, not only Korean are China-hungry.
European financial institutions, particularly German banks, are keen on China debt issue, another banker said.
Elsewhere in Asia, Thai Farmers Bank has authorised ABN Amro to arrange a US$125 million five-year loan facility.
The loan pays an interest margin of 27 basis points over the LIBOR.
In South Korea, Asian Banking Corporation and Daegu Bank are rumoured to be lining up for their respective new debt issues.
